scenes.tts: Plot the pressure inside the left ventricle against its volume. Each heartbeat then draws a closed loop. This is a model adult ventricle at rest, with made up numbers. It has four corners, and an area inside. When the arteries tighten, which corner moves?
scenes.visual: Empty axes of ventricular pressure against volume; a dot traces the closed loop; four question marks sit on the corners; an orange 'arteries tighten' label points at the loop.

scenes.tts: The beat runs counterclockwise. At the bottom right, the mitral valve closes. That volume is the end diastolic volume, one hundred twenty five millilitres. Pressure now rises with the volume fixed. At about eighty millimetres of mercury, the aortic valve opens and the ventricle ejects. At the top left, the aortic valve closes. That volume is the end systolic volume, forty five millilitres, at one hundred twenty millimetres of mercury. Pressure then falls with the volume fixed. The mitral valve opens, and the ventricle fills.
scenes.visual: A dot runs round the loop counterclockwise; each corner's question mark becomes its valve event, and the volumes and pressures are marked on the axes.
scenes.caption: The beat runs counterclockwise. At the bottom right, the mitral valve closes. That volume is the end-diastolic volume, 125 mL. Pressure now rises with the volume fixed. At about 80 mmHg, the aortic valve opens and the ventricle ejects. At the top left, the aortic valve closes. That volume is the end-systolic volume, 45 mL, at 120 mmHg. Pressure then falls with the volume fixed. The mitral valve opens, and the ventricle fills.

scenes.tts: The width of the loop is the stroke volume. One hundred twenty five minus forty five is eighty millilitres. Divide eighty by one hundred twenty five, and the ejection fraction is sixty four percent. The area inside the loop is the stroke work of the beat.
scenes.visual: A yellow arrow spans the loop's width under the volume axis; the sums for stroke volume and ejection fraction appear; the loop fills as the stroke work.
scenes.caption: The width of the loop is the stroke volume. 125 minus 45 is 80 mL. Divide 80 by 125, and the ejection fraction is 64 percent. The area inside the loop is the stroke work of the beat.
scenes.narration: The width of the loop is the stroke volume. 125 minus 45 is 80 mL. Divide 80 by 125, and the ejection fraction is 64 percent. The area inside the loop is the stroke work of the beat.

scenes.tts: The top left corner lies on a line, the end systolic pressure volume relation. Its slope, E E S, is a relatively load independent index of contractility. Here E E S is three millimetres of mercury per millilitre, and the line meets the volume axis at five millilitres. A second line starts at the end diastolic volume and runs to the corner. Its steepness is the effective arterial elastance, E A, here one point five. The corner sits where the two lines meet.
scenes.visual: A green line is drawn up from the volume axis; an orange line is drawn from the end-diastolic volume to the corner; the corner is marked; a readout panel fills with the model's numbers.
scenes.caption: The top left corner lies on a line, the end-systolic pressure-volume relation. Its slope, Ees, is a relatively load-independent index of contractility. Here Ees is 3 mmHg per mL, and the line meets the volume axis at 5 mL. A second line starts at the end-diastolic volume and runs to the corner. Its steepness is the effective arterial elastance, Ea, here 1.5. The corner sits where the two lines meet.
scenes.narration: The top left corner lies on a line, the end-systolic pressure-volume relation. Its slope, Ees, is a relatively load-independent index of contractility. Here Ees is 3 mmHg per mL, and the line meets the volume axis at 5 mL. A second line starts at the end-diastolic volume and runs to the corner. scenes.tts: Now tighten the arteries, and hold filling and contractility fixed. In the model, arteriolar constriction raises E A to two. The steeper line meets the same end systolic line higher up. End systolic pressure rises to one hundred forty four millimetres of mercury. End systolic volume rises to fifty three millilitres. Stroke volume falls to seventy two. Ejection fraction falls to fifty seven point six percent.
scenes.visual: The orange line pivots steeper about the end-diastolic volume; the corner slides up the unchanged green line; the readouts update and the stroke-volume arrow shortens.
scenes.caption: Now tighten the arteries, and hold filling and contractility fixed. In the model, arteriolar constriction raises Ea to 2. The steeper line meets the same end-systolic line higher up. End-systolic pressure rises to 144 mmHg. End-systolic volume rises to 53 mL. Stroke volume falls to 72. Ejection fraction falls to 57.6 percent.
scenes.narration: Now tighten the arteries, and hold filling and contractility fixed. In the model, arteriolar constriction raises Ea to 2. The steeper line meets the same end-systolic line higher up. End-systolic pressure rises to 144 mmHg. End-systolic volume rises to 53 mL. Stroke volume falls to 72. scenes.tts: Filling and contractility did not change, yet ejection fraction fell. So ejection fraction can change with no change in contractility. Go back to the first loop. Raise filling to one hundred forty millilitres, and the corner slides up the same line. Stroke volume rises to ninety. Now return filling to one hundred twenty five, and raise E E S to four point five. The line steepens, and end systolic volume falls to thirty five. The rule to keep: preload, afterload and contractility each move a different part of the loop.
scenes.visual: Back to baseline: the end-diastolic volume moves right and the corner slides up the green line; then the green line steepens and the corner drops; the rule ends the film.
scenes.caption: Filling and contractility did not change, yet ejection fraction fell. So ejection fraction can change with no change in contractility. Go back to the first loop. Raise filling to 140 mL, and the corner slides up the same line. Stroke volume rises to 90. Now return filling to 125, and raise Ees to 4.5. The line steepens, and end-systolic volume falls to 35. The rule to keep: preload, afterload and contractility each move a different part of the loop.
